title: Prior Authorization: Process and Pitfalls
summary: Prior authorization is a payer requirement that certain services receive advance approval before delivery — a major administrative burden with significant revenue implications.
objectives: Describe the prior authorization process and its key steps
Identify the services most commonly requiring authorization
Explain how authorization failures lead to denials and strategies to prevent them

content_blocks.body:
Prior authorization (PA) — also called pre-authorization, pre-certification, or pre-approval — is a requirement that providers obtain payer approval before delivering certain services. Without authorization, payers may deny the claim regardless of medical necessity.

Services most commonly requiring PA include:
- Inpatient admissions (especially elective surgeries)
- High-cost imaging (MRI, CT, PET scans)
- Specialty drugs and infusion therapy
- Durable medical equipment (DME)
- Outpatient procedures (certain interventional services)
- Behavioral health services beyond initial visits

content_blocks.body: CMS finalized rules requiring payers to implement FHIR-based APIs for prior authorization by 2026 (Interoperability and Prior Authorization Final Rule, CMS-0057-F). This will enable electronic, near-real-time PA decisions for many services, reducing the current 1–14 day wait times for manual PA requests.
